dye.e: From Middle English deye, from Old English dēah, dēag (“color, hue, dye”), from Proto-West Germanic *daugu (“color, shade”), from *daugan (“to conceal, be dark”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰewh₂- (“to smoke, raise dust, camouflage”).
dye.g: A colorant, especially one that has an affinity to the substrate to which it is applied.

dye.e: Fom Middle English deien, from Old English dēagian, from the noun.
dye.g: To colour with dye, or as if with dye.

dying.g: Approaching death; about to die; moribund.

dynasty.e: Borrowed from Middle French dynastie, from Late Latin dynastia, from Ancient Greek δυναστεία (dunasteía, “power, dominion”).
dynasty.g: A series of rulers or dynasts from one family.

dysentery.e: From Middle English dissenterie, from Old French dissenterie, from Latin dysenteria, from Ancient Greek δυσεντερία (dusentería), from δυσ- (dus-, “bad”) + ἔντερα (éntera, “bowels”).
